capture.final_message:
Use the Carathéodory splitting identity as the central mechanism.

For the first conjunct, apply `h₁` to  
\(A=t\cap(s₁\cup s₂)\). It gives
\[
m(A)=m(A\cap s₁)+m(A\setminus s₁).
\]
Then use \(s₁\cap s₂=\varnothing\) to establish the set identities
\[
A\cap s₁=t\cap s₁,\qquad A\setminus s₁=t\cap s₂.
\]
Substitution yields the desired equality.

For the second conjunct, unfold `OuterMeasure.IsCaratheodory`. Its defining equality is equivalent to the displayed reverse inequality because outer-measure subadditivity always supplies
\[
m(t)\le m(t\cap s)+m(t\setminus s),
\]
using \(t=(t\cap s)\cup(t\setminus s)\). Combine this universal inequality with the assumed opposite inequality by antisymmetry. The only essential ingredient is outer-measure subadditivity; no measurability assumption on \(s\) is needed for that direction.
